text.p: Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy on Thursday declined to say whether it would renew its bid for Canadian paper maker Repap Enterprises Inc.

"UPM-Kymmene has no reason to comment on this situation," UPM chief spokesman Markku Franssila said by telephone after news that a proposed acquisition of Repap by Canadian pulp and paper maker Avenor Inc was rejected by Avenor shareholders.
On Tuesday, UPM-Kymmene said it had bid for parts of Repap late last year but that the bid had become void when Repap received another offer.
On Wednesday, Avenor shareholders rejected the company's proposed C$2.6 billion ($1.9 billion) acquisition of Repap.
Repap shareholders approved the deal at a separate meeting.
A third Canadian paper producer, Domtar Inc, has said it is also interested in pursuing a three-way merger with Avenor and Repap.
Earlier this month, UPM-Kymmene said it planned to enter a paper-coating technology pact with Domtar.
Franssila declined to comment on whether UPM-Kymmene had any plans for a move into North America, either by way of corporate acquisitions or otherwise.
UPM-Kymmene, Europe's biggest forest industry group, has said it plans to become a global paper producer.
